title: Configure network devices for remote access using SSH

questions.question: Identify required before generating the encryption keys for SSH on a router or switch?
choices: Setting the hostname and domain name

correct.explanation: SSH RSA key generation requires ip domain-name (with hostname set) — the FQDN labels the key pair.

incorrect.explanation: Accurate clock/NTP helps certificate validation but hostname + domain-name are required before crypto key generate rsa.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Time/date as only SSH key prerequisite
incorrect.whatItDoes: Setting the time and date points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for identify.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "identify", Setting the hostname and domain name satisfies what this question tests — Setting the time and date does not.

incorrect.explanation: Key modulus size is specified during generation — not a separate prerequisite step.
incorrect.whatItDoes: Setting the key strength points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for identify.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "identify", Setting the hostname and domain name satisfies what this question tests — Setting the key strength does not.

incorrect.explanation: No key repository config exists — set hostname and ip domain-name first.
incorrect.whatItDoes: Setting the key repository points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for identify.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "identify", Setting the hostname and domain name satisfies what this question tests — Setting the key repository does not.

answerReview.examTip: SSH key prep: hostname R1 → ip domain-name lab.local → crypto key generate rsa.

questions.question: Which command enable SSH version 2 for logins?

correct.explanation: ip ssh version 2 in global config forces SSHv2 — more secure than SSHv1.

incorrect.explanation: SSH version is global config, not config-line — use ip ssh version 2.
incorrect.whatItDoes: Router(config-line)#version 2 points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for ssh.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "ssh", Router(config)#ip ssh version 2 satisfies what this question tests — Router(config-line)#version 2 does not.

incorrect.explanation: config-ssh is not a valid config mode — ip ssh version 2 is global.
incorrect.whatItDoes: Router(config-ssh)#version 2 points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for ssh.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "ssh", Router(config)#ip ssh version 2 satisfies what this question tests — Router(config-ssh)#version 2 does not.

incorrect.explanation: Correct syntax is ip ssh version 2, not ssh version 2.
incorrect.whatItDoes: Router(config)#ssh version 2 points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for ssh.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "ssh", Router(config)#ip ssh version 2 satisfies what this question tests — Router(config)#ssh version 2 does not.

answerReview.examTip: SSH harden: ip ssh version 2 + transport input ssh on vty lines + disable Telnet.

questions.question: Which command configure the router or switch to allow SSH as a protocol for management with a fallback of Telnet?

correct.explanation: transport input ssh telnet under line vty allows SSH with Telnet fallback — configure after generating keys for SSH.

incorrect.explanation: login ssh telnet is not valid global config — transport protocols are set under line vty.
incorrect.whatItDoes: Switch(config)#login ssh telnet uses cleartext Telnet for remote device management.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: Device management (configure): Switch(config-line)#transport ssh telnet protects credentials in transit — Switch(config)#login ssh telnet uses cleartext remote access.

incorrect.explanation: login controls authentication method — allowed protocols are set with transport input on the line.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Using login instead of transport input
incorrect.whatItDoes: Switch(config-line)#login ssh telnet uses cleartext Telnet for remote device management.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: Device management (configure): Switch(config-line)#transport ssh telnet protects credentials in transit — Switch(config-line)#login ssh telnet uses cleartext remote access.

incorrect.explanation: transport input must be under config-line — global config#transport is wrong context.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Setting transport input at wrong config level
incorrect.whatItDoes: Switch(config)#transport ssh telnet uses cleartext Telnet for remote device management.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: Device management (configure): Switch(config-line)#transport ssh telnet protects credentials in transit — Switch(config)#transport ssh telnet uses cleartext remote access.

answerReview.examTip: VTY: transport input ssh telnet under line vty (after ip domain-name + crypto key).

questions.question: Why should Telnet be replaced with SSH?
choices: SSH makes it easier to create ACLs for access.

correct.explanation: Replace Telnet with SSH because SSH encrypts the entire management session — credentials and commands are protected.

incorrect.explanation: Telnet has no encryption (not weak encryption) — all traffic is cleartext.
incorrect.whatItDoes: Telnet has weak encryption. uses cleartext Telnet for remote device management.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: Device management (replaced): SSH is encrypted. protects credentials in transit — Telnet has weak encryption. uses cleartext remote access.

incorrect.explanation: File copy uses SCP/FTP/TFTP — not the primary reason to replace Telnet with SSH.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: SSH for file copy over Telnet replacement
incorrect.whatItDoes: SSH allows for file copy. points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for replaced.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "replaced", SSH is encrypted. satisfies what this question tests — SSH allows for file copy. does not.

incorrect.explanation: ACLs control who connects — SSH adds encryption regardless of ACL rules.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: SSH eases ACL creation as main benefit
incorrect.whatItDoes: SSH makes it easier to create ACLs for access. points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for replaced.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "replaced", SSH is encrypted. satisfies what this question tests — SSH makes it easier to create ACLs for access. does not.

answerReview.examTip: Telnet = cleartext TCP/23 | SSH = encrypted TCP/22 — always prefer SSH on vty lines.

questions.question: You have created the SSH encryption keys, but you cannot enable SSH version 2. What is the problem?
choices: The time and date need to be corrected.
The key strength needs to be 768 bits or higher.
The DNS server is not configured.
There is no host record for the switch or router.

correct.explanation: SSHv2 requires RSA keys of at least 768 bits (1024+ recommended) — shorter keys block v2 enablement.

incorrect.explanation: Clock/NTP affects logs and certs — it does not block ip ssh version 2 like key size does.
incorrect.whatItDoes: The time and date need to be corrected. points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for encryption.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "encryption", The key strength needs to be 768 bits or higher. satisfies what this question tests — The time and date need to be corrected. does not.

incorrect.explanation: DNS is not required for SSHv2 — insufficient RSA modulus prevents v2.
incorrect.whatItDoes: The DNS server is not configured. points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for encryption.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "encryption", The key strength needs to be 768 bits or higher. satisfies what this question tests — The DNS server is not configured. does not.

incorrect.explanation: No DNS host record is needed on the device — key modulus ≥ 768 is the v2 requirement.
incorrect.whatItDoes: There is no host record for the switch or router. points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for encryption.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "encryption", The key strength needs to be 768 bits or higher. satisfies what this question tests — There is no host record for the switch or router. does not.

answerReview.examTip: SSHv2 key: crypto key generate rsa modulus 1024 (or 2048) — v2 fails with tiny keys.

questions.question: Which command configure a local user for SSH access?

correct.explanation: username <name> password <secret> creates a local user database entry for login authentication.

incorrect.explanation: account is not valid IOS — local users use username in global config.
incorrect.whatItDoes: Router(config)#account user1 Router(config-acct)#password Password20! points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for configure.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "configure", Router(config)#username user1 password Password20! satisfies what this question tests — Router(config)#account user1 Router(config-acct)#password Password20! does not.

incorrect.explanation: user alone is incomplete — correct syntax is username <name> password <pwd>.
incorrect.whatItDoes: Router(config)#user user1 Password20! points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for configure.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "configure", Router(config)#username user1 password Password20! satisfies what this question tests — Router(config)#user user1 Password20! does not.

incorrect.explanation: user-account is not valid Cisco syntax — use username.
incorrect.whatItDoes: Router(config)#user-account user1 password Password20! points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for configure.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "configure", Router(config)#username user1 password Password20! satisfies what this question tests — Router(config)#user-account user1 password Password20! does not.

answerReview.examTip: Local auth: username bob secret <pwd> (preferred over plaintext password) + login local on vty.

questions.question: Which command generate the encryption keys for SSH?

correct.explanation: crypto key generate rsa in global config creates the RSA key pair used by SSH.

incorrect.explanation: Keyword order is crypto key generate rsa, not generate crypto key rsa.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Wrong crypto key command word order
incorrect.whatItDoes: Router(config)#generate crypto key rsa points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for generate.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "generate", Router(config)#crypto key generate rsa satisfies what this question tests — Router(config)#generate crypto key rsa does not.

incorrect.explanation: crypto generate key rsa reverses the middle keywords — use crypto key generate rsa.
incorrect.whatItDoes: Router(config)#crypto generate key rsa points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for generate.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "generate", Router(config)#crypto key generate rsa satisfies what this question tests — Router(config)#crypto generate key rsa does not.

incorrect.explanation: Key generation is global config (Router(config)#), not privileged EXEC alone.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: RSA key generation in exec mode
incorrect.whatItDoes: Router#crypto key generate rsa points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for generate.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "generate", Router(config)#crypto key generate rsa satisfies what this question tests — Router#crypto key generate rsa does not.

answerReview.examTip: SSH keys: crypto key generate rsa → confirm with show ip ssh.

questions.question: You want to turn on local authentication so that a user must supply a username and password when managing the switch. You have created the username and password combinations on the switch. Which command direct SSH and Telnet to use this authentication model?

correct.explanation: login local under line vty tells SSH/Telnet to authenticate against the local username database.

incorrect.explanation: aaa new-model enables AAA framework — local-only auth uses login local on the line.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: aaa new-model for simple local login
incorrect.whatItDoes: Switch(config)#new aaa model points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for managing the switch.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "managing the switch", Switch(config-line)#login local satisfies what this question tests — Switch(config)#new aaa model does not.

incorrect.explanation: local authentication is not a global command — use login local under line vty.
incorrect.whatItDoes: Switch(config)#local authentication points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for managing the switch.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "managing the switch", Switch(config-line)#login local satisfies what this question tests — Switch(config)#local authentication does not.

incorrect.explanation: local authentication is not valid under config-line — the command is login local.
incorrect.whatItDoes: Switch(config-line)#local authentication points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for managing the switch.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "managing the switch", Switch(config-line)#login local satisfies what this question tests — Switch(config-line)#local authentication does not.

answerReview.examTip: VTY auth chain: create username → line vty 0 4 → login local → transport input ssh.

questions.question: Which banner will be displayed first when a user connects to a Cisco device via SSH?

correct.explanation: The login banner (banner login) displays first when a user connects — before authentication prompts.

incorrect.explanation: MOTD banner shows at more connection types but login banner precedes it for SSH login sequence per Cisco order.
incorrect.whatItDoes: MOTD banner points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for a user connects to a Cisco device via SSH.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "a user connects to a Cisco device via SSH", Login banner satisfies what this question tests — MOTD banner does not.

incorrect.explanation: Exec banner displays after successful login — not on initial connection.
incorrect.whatItDoes: Exec banner points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for a user connects to a Cisco device via SSH.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "a user connects to a Cisco device via SSH", Login banner satisfies what this question tests — Exec banner does not.

incorrect.explanation: Incoming banner is for reverse-Telnet lines — standard SSH uses login banner first.
incorrect.whatItDoes: Incoming banner points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for a user connects to a Cisco device via SSH.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "a user connects to a Cisco device via SSH", Login banner satisfies what this question tests — Incoming banner does not.

answerReview.examTip: Banner order on connect: login → credentials → MOTD (if set) → exec (after auth).
